mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate accommodative policy easing.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods with FEDFUNDS declining for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: FEDFUNDS exceeding 4.5% for two consecutive months signals restrictive monetary policy, increasing equity discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >45% of periods with FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 2 consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous 0.5% monthly increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days via accelerated earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >55% of instances where HOUST and RSAFS both rise >0.5% monthly, or interaction effect p-value > 0.05 in regression model.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.5%), rising payroll employment (PAYEMS growth > 0.3% monthly) signals wage inflation pressures, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as rate hike expectations rise.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >45% of periods with UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.3% monthly, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 6-month decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) correlates with improving labor market conditions, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through rising corporate profits.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods with UNRATE declining for 6 consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: INDPRO falling below 95.0 for two consecutive months signals manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate earnings growth and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >45% of periods with INDPRO < 95.0 for 2 consecutive months, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous INDPRO decline and FEDFUNDS rise (>0.25%) signal dual economic shock of manufacturing slowdown and monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >55% of instances with INDPRO decline and FEDFUNDS rise >0.25%, or interaction effect p-value > 0.05 in regression model.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized), rising GDP growth (GDPC1 growth > 0.5% quarterly) indicates strong economic expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days via growth-oriented equity revaluation.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods with CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized and GDPC1 growth > 0.5% quarterly, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.
